As for new activities, just one: I found a page that simulates how a miner tests hashes to find the correct one and mine a block. The page shows which and how many times a hash was created to reach the correct one. It’s something dynamic that would help students see the computational power required for mining.

The second point isn’t an activity on its own, but it could be added to one. In the fractional reserve exercise, a participant could take on the role of a saver, and with a table, we could clearly explain how their savings decrease in value as a percentage due to money issuance.

column9:
Teaching people about Bitcoin who really want to learn, who have the intrinsic motivation and who are curious. I loved the vivid discussion and how fast we made progress. I loved seeing them evolve and day week by week, asking more questions about how to USE BITCOIN or e.g if we can do a P2P transaction. Some of the students really changed their lives after the graduation, completely changed their mind set, some quitting their fiat job to get involved in Bitcoin (some even in our team) or thinking about how to implement Bitcoin in their current job (e.g. by accepting Bitcoin as form of payment). I really enjoyed the energy in our class, the playful, interactive way of teaching. I loved how I also got very passionate about teaching. 

Also it was great that the program gives us the freedom to change it in the way we think is best for our community, e.g through activities, examples, class structure.
